title: Returns Desk Guidance — Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card When Its Qualifying Purchase Comes Back
content:
A Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card, one of the Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards, was earned by a qualifying purchase of at least the kind's qualifying purchase amount, and the Bonus Card value issued per qualifying purchase step is the kind's bonus value. When that qualifying purchase is returned so that the kept merchandise falls below the qualifying purchase amount, an unused Bonus Card is forfeited in full, booked as a forfeiture that names the return, and a Bonus Card already used has the value used deducted from the refund of the return. No forfeiture has already been booked for the same return. The forfeiture rule applies only to a card kind whose forfeit-on-qualifying-return term is yes.

## Conditions and results

| Condition | Read from |
|---|---|
| The card kind's forfeit-on-qualifying-return term is yes | The card kind |
| The returned merchandise belongs to the purchase that earned the Bonus Card | The return and the qualifying purchase on record |
| After the return, the merchandise kept from that purchase is below the qualifying purchase amount | The qualifying purchase and its returns |
| No forfeiture has already been booked for the same return | The Bonus Card's entries, looked up by that return |

| State of the Bonus Card when the conditions hold | Result |
|---|---|
| Unused | Forfeited in full; the forfeiture names the return |
| Already used | The value used is deducted from the refund of the return |

## One forfeiture per return

A forfeiture already booked on the card's record for a given return settles that return: no second forfeiture is booked for the same return. The check is made on the card's own entries, matched by the return.

## Hypothetical cases

The cases below use the Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card kind's qualifying purchase amount of $100.00 and bonus value of $20.00; the purchases and returns are hypothetical.

- A hypothetical qualifying purchase of $160.00 earned an unused $20.00 Bonus Card. $70.00 of it is returned, leaving $90.00 kept, which is below $100.00. The Bonus Card is forfeited in full, $20.00, and the forfeiture names that return.
- A hypothetical qualifying purchase of $130.00 earned a Bonus Card whose $20.00 has been spent in full. $40.00 of it is returned, leaving $90.00 kept, below $100.00. The $20.00 used is deducted from the refund of that return, so the refund is $40.00 less $20.00, which is $20.00.
- For the first case, a forfeiture already appears on the card's record naming the same return: no further forfeiture is booked for that return.
